prompt.context: Our client is a private equity firm interested in Molds R Us, a small company that makes plastic moldings for houses in Russia. The firm wants to know if investing in this company is a good idea. They also want to understand what the 2011 market for moldings, particularly in plastics, will look like.
prompt.question: Should the PE firm invest in Molds R Us? What will the 2011 market for plastic moldings look like?

clarifying_info.q: What growth rate does the PE firm require?
clarifying_info.a: The PE firm wants to see growth of 20% in the first year to justify this purchase.

clarifying_info.q: Is the company considering international expansion?
clarifying_info.a: This company only plays in the Russian market and the PE firm is not interested in expanding across borders.

clarifying_info.q: Does Molds R Us compete with other plastic molding companies?
clarifying_info.a: This company is the only player in plastic moldings.
Moldings are used where walls meet the ceiling to add a decorative appeal to houses and are only used in residential buildings.

clarifying_info.q: When do housing starts require moldings?
clarifying_info.a: All housing starts require molding in the year they are started, and are all completed by the next year.

exhibits.title: Molding Options
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of molding types available in Russia, showing price, installation requirements, and replacement frequency for each type, plus general contractor and house dimensions data.

data.other: Contractor lays 1000 feet of molding per hour; contractor earns 50 Rubles/hour; average house has 4000 meters of walls

exhibits.title: Moldings Used in the Russian Market
exhibits.shows: A stacked bar chart showing market share of each molding type from 2005 to 2010, alongside a table of total residences and housing starts per year.

framework: Market sizing: estimate size and growth of the overall Russian moldings market
Competitive landscape: identify market share by molding type and trend over time
Client positioning: Molds R Us is the sole plastic moldings player — assess plastic's share trajectory
Growth analysis: project 2011 plastic molding demand and compare to the 20% growth hurdle
Investment recommendation: evaluate whether the business can meet the PE firm's return threshold
Next steps: identify levers if the base case falls short

questions.prompt: Size the 2011 market for plastic (PVC) moldings in meters.
questions.guidance: Strong answer multiplies 2011 total residences (2010 residences + 2010 starts) by plastic market share to get stock of plastic-molding homes, applies a 1/5 replacement rate to that stock, adds new 2011 starts multiplied by plastic share, then converts houses to meters using 4000 m/house. Key insight: ~85% of demand comes from existing homes replacing moldings, only ~15% from new construction.

math.setup: 2011 total residences = 2010 residences + 2010 starts; plastic stock = total residences × 25% plastic share; annual replacements = plastic stock / 5; new plastic starts = 2011 estimated starts × 25%; total houses = replacements + new starts; total meters = total houses × 4000 m
steps: 2011 estimated starts ≈ 1.4M (extrapolation of trend); new plastic demand = 1.4M × 25% = 0.35M houses
math.answer: Approximately 8.2 billion meters of plastic moldings sold in 2011

questions.prompt: Does this volume support a 20% revenue growth target for the PE firm?
questions.guidance: Candidate should compare 2011 projected demand against implied 2010 baseline, note that plastic market share is flat at 25% (2005–2010), and conclude that growth is driven only by housing starts — which are far below 20% year-over-year. The PE firm's 20% hurdle is not achievable with organic market growth alone.

math.setup: Estimate 2010 plastic molding demand using same methodology and compare to 2011
math.answer: Plastic molding market grows roughly 8% year-over-year, far short of the 20% growth target

brainstorming.prompt: If the base case falls short of 20% growth, what next steps should the PE firm consider?

categories.name: Alternative acquisition targets
ideas: Look at rubber molding companies — rubber market share has grown from 11% (2005) to 16% (2010), showing the fastest share growth of any segment
Evaluate wood or plaster molding players for consolidation opportunity

categories.name: Revenue growth levers for Molds R Us
ideas: Invest in sales and marketing to capture share from 'no molding' homes (still 45% of market)
Expand distribution channels or sales force to reach underserved regions
Introduce product line extensions (e.g., premium plastic designs) to upsell existing customers

categories.name: Operational improvements
ideas: Reduce cost per meter to improve margins even if volume growth is modest
Invest in contractor partnerships to ease installation barriers and stimulate demand

recommendation: The PE firm should NOT purchase Molds R Us under current conditions.
Plastic molding market share has been essentially flat at 25% from 2005 to 2010, and overall housing growth yields only ~8% volume growth — well below the 20% first-year hurdle.
The majority of demand (~85%) comes from replacement cycles in existing homes, not from new construction, so incremental housing starts provide limited upside.
risks: If Russian housing starts accelerate beyond the trend, demand growth could be higher than modeled.
If Molds R Us can capture share from 'no molding' homes, revenue growth could exceed base case.
Macro risk: Russian housing market could slow, compressing even the 8% baseline.
next_steps: Evaluate rubber molding companies as acquisition targets — rubber is the fastest-growing segment by market share.
Conduct commercial due diligence on Molds R Us's sales and marketing capabilities to assess whether a 20% growth plan is executable.
Model scenarios where plastic captures additional share from 'no molding' households to stress-test the bull case.
